articles.title: Rochdale projects £10.6 million spending on roads as repair programme targets borough streets
articles.excerpt: Council figures project £10.63 million in carriageway maintenance spending for 2026/27, around 26 per cent more than the previous year.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council projects spending £10.63 million on carriageway maintenance this financial year, around £2.16 million more than the previous year.

The figures appear in the council’s Highways Maintenance Transparency Report, which sets out how it maintains the borough’s roads and where the money goes.

Projected carriageway spending for 2026/27 is approximately 26 per cent higher than the £8.47 million recorded for 2025/26. The total includes £1.357 million in Department for Transport incentive funding.

The £10.63 million covers carriageway maintenance across the borough, including wider repairs and resurfacing. It is a spending projection for the full financial year, rather than a sum already spent.

The council’s capital programme lists 6.01 kilometres of road resurfacing and a further 7.10 kilometres of preventative treatment.

Named resurfacing locations include Whitegates Road in Middleton, Wordsworth Way and Seymour Street in Heywood, Belfield Lane, Kiln Lane and sections of Edenfield Road.

The report also records 10,998 permanent repairs and 364 temporary repairs during 2025/26, illustrating the scale of ongoing maintenance. Those figures count repairs rather than individual streets.

For residents, the practical question is what improvement that spending will deliver on the roads they use every day.

Which street should be a priority, and have previous repairs lasted? Tell us the road name and nearest junction in the comments so we can investigate specific locations.

articles.title: Plans to develop wasteland around Rochdale train station confirmed
articles.excerpt: Plans to transform the wasteland surrounding Rochdale train station into a usable space have been confirmed, marking a significant step towards improving the area.
articles.content_html:
Plans to develop the wasteland around Rochdale train station have been confirmed. Local authorities aim to enhance the environment and accessibility for commuters and residents.

This initiative is part of ongoing efforts to revitalise the area, which has been largely neglected in recent years. The local council stated that the project will improve aesthetic appeal and provide additional facilities for the community.

Specific details regarding the timeline and nature of the developments are yet to be announced. Stakeholders are optimistic that this project will lead to increased foot traffic and economic activity in the vicinity of the station.

Residents and commuters are encouraged to monitor the progress of this project, as it is expected to positively impact local transport and community engagement.

evidence_sources.captured_text: The wasteland around Rochdale train station is finally being put to use - Manchester Evening News ‌ ‌ Skip to main content Manchester Evening News: Number one for news, opinion, sport & celebrity news The wasteland around Rochdale train station is finally being put to use The regeneration around the railway station is part of a wider vision to improve the flow of the down and drive investment Add to preferred sources Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 06:13, 21 Oct 2026 View 4 Images Land surrounding Rochdale train station (Image: LDRS) A scheme which would transform the gateway into Rochdale is making significant progress, town hall bosses say. ‌ ‌ Some 81 two, three-and four-bedroom homes are currently under construction on vacant land next to Rochdale ’s Central Retail Park. This forms part of a wider scheme to create a connection between the train station and the town centre. ‌ The wider regeneration of the area around Rochdale railway station also involves the creation of a new public square in front of the station and 33 new apartments on a brownfield site on the corner of Maclure Road and Station Road. ‌ Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The train station in Rochdale was once a hub for industrial business generations ago, so the distance between the station and the town centre was purposeful separation. But as times changed, society changed and the station suddenly started transporting people, not goods. This is why there is an idea to improve access and avenues from the station and the main hub of the town. This 81-home development, known as John Rennie Place, in honour of the late Scottish Civil engineer who masterminded the Rochdale Canal, got under way in November last year, and is due for completion in December 2027. ‌ View 4 Images The former Central Retail Park site development under construction (Image: Rochdale council) The project, approved years ago, was unlocked following a successful bid for £15m from the government’s Community Regeneration Partnerships Fund. The transformation has been on the cards for a long time, but the local authority struggled to get the investment until last year. ‌ The properties will be the first affordable net zero homes delivered as part of a housing scheme supported by the council. The local authority says the development is already delivering benefits to the local economy and community. Contractor Willmott Dixon, working on behalf of the council, has already spent £3.3m with local civil engineering firm, Hovington Ltd, and supported a total of 95 weeks of apprenticeship and T-Level training, including three T-Level placements from Hopwood Hall College. ‌ Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Seven local people are also employed on the project, including two people who were previously unemployed, with the council’s work and skills team supporting the recruitment. ‌ Tommy Patterson, 22, from Middleton , is one of the local people working on the new homes. He said: “I had been out of work for six months when the job centre arranged for me to get my CSCS card and that led to me securing a scaffolding apprenticeship here on site. I have always worked and had been let go, so getting this job was a lifeline. “I live on my own and I was struggling to pay my bills. It’s great to work here. Everyone is lovely; it’s a smashing team.” ‌ View 4 Images Councillor Danny Meredith looking across the former Rochdale Central Retail Park site (Image: Rochdale council) Daniel Fletcher, 17, is studying for a T Level in design, surveying and planning at Hopwood Hall College, said: “I really like it here. I’ve been talking to the different trades delivering this project, so I’ve been exposed to different parts of the job, and I have the freedom to go onto site on my own. It’s already changed massively since I started in the summer.” ‌ The project is being led by Rochdale Development Agency (RDA) on behalf of Rochdale Borough Council. Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for housing and regeneration at Rochdale Borough Council, said: ”We want local people and businesses to feel the benefit of local projects and it’s great to see that these benefits are already being felt on this development before a single house has even been completed. ‌ View 4 Images Councillor Danny Meredith looking across the former Rochdale Central Retail Park site (Image: Rochdale council) “By ensuring that social value is embedded in our procurement system, we’re making sure that local people are invested in the extensive regeneration which is taking place on their doorstep and are benefitting from the economic transformation we’re spearheading across the borough. That’s how it should be and how it will continue to be.” Article continues below Work to create 142 apartments next to the new homes is ongoing, with the procurement of a delivery partner expected to get underway soon. articles.title: Office of Rail and Road rejects proposal for extra Rochdale to London train services
articles.excerpt: The Office of Rail and Road has turned down a proposal for additional train services from Rochdale to London, citing concerns over delays and capacity on the West Coast Main Line.
articles.content_html:
Plans to enhance the rail link between Rochdale and London have been rejected once again. The Office of Rail and Road (ORR) announced that it had turned down proposals from Lumo to operate up to four additional return services from Rochdale to Euston on weekdays and Saturdays, and three services on Sundays.

Rochdale MP Paul Waugh had supported the bid, describing it as a "game-changing opportunity" for the borough and the wider North West. However, the ORR's assessment concluded that adding more trains to the already congested West Coast Main Line would likely lead to increased delays and cancellations for passengers. This decision follows a similar rejection of Lumo's application last year, with the ORR stating that the capacity and performance of the southern section of the line had not materially changed since then.

An external review commissioned by the ORR corroborated these findings, indicating that the current timetable must allow for recovery time during disruptions to minimise delays. The ORR emphasised the importance of maintaining service reliability for existing passengers.

The rejection of this proposal means that residents of Rochdale will not see an increase in direct train services to London in the near future, which could impact travel options for commuters and those wishing to visit the capital.

evidence_sources.captured_text: New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused Plans to improve the rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again. Today, the Office of Rail and Road announced it had rejected proposals for new train services which would have seen Lumo operate up to four additional return Rochdale-to-Euston services on weekdays and Saturdays and three services on Sundays . Among those backing calls for the extra services was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who called Lumo’s bid to restore six daily direct services between Rochdale and the capital a “game-changing opportunity” for the borough and the wider North West. But the ORR rejected the plans after its assessment found adding more trains to the West Coast Main Line — which also included services to Blackpool and Wrexham — would likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers. It said its assessment following detailed and extensive analysis is that the capacity and performance of the southern section of the West Coast Main Line has not materially changed since it rejected a similar application by Lumo last year. An external review commissioned by ORR also supported this conclusion. READ MORE: Police target crime gang’s ‘spider web of criminality’ The ORR said gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers. It concluded that adding more services into these windows in the timetable for recovery would reduce that resilience, increasing the risk of disruption spreading to other services and affecting more passengers. Stephanie Tobyn, ORR’s director of strategy, policy and reform, said: “New services, destinations and greater choice can bring real benefits for passengers and communities. “But the West Coast Main Line is already under significant pressure, with performance reflecting limited resilience on a heavily used part of the rail network. “Our detailed analysis has shown that adding more trains to the current timetable would reduce the ability to recover when disruption occurs, increasing the risk of delays spreading and making reliability of the network worse for all passengers.” SUPPORT THE ROCHDALE TIMES: FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK Got a story? articles.title: Lifts out of service at Freehold Tram Stop due to replacement works
articles.excerpt: The lifts at Freehold Tram Stop are currently out of service as replacement works take place, affecting passengers travelling towards Manchester and Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
The lifts at Freehold Tram Stop are currently out of service, impacting passengers using the tram service towards Manchester and Rochdale. The disruption began on Saturday, 24 October 2026, at 10:19 am and will continue until further notice as lift replacement works are carried out.

Passengers are advised to alight at either South Chadderton or Westwood tram stops and use the orange call points located at all stops to request assistance for completing their journeys. For further assistance, customers can contact the helpline at 0161 244 1000, which operates from 7 am to 8 pm on weekdays and from 8 am to 8 pm on weekends and bank holidays.

This service disruption may affect those who rely on the tram for daily commutes or travel to local amenities. It is advisable for passengers to plan their journeys accordingly and consider alternative routes during this period.

Updates regarding the status of the lifts and any further developments will be provided through the Bee Network travel alerts. Passengers are encouraged to check the latest information as the situation evolves.

articles.title: Delays on Rochdale East Didsbury line due to track obstruction
articles.excerpt: Tram services on the Rochdale East Didsbury line are delayed following an obstruction on the tracks, with further disruptions across the network due to a road traffic collision.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has reported delays on the Rochdale East Didsbury tram line due to an object blocking the tracks. The disruption was noted on Tuesday, 13 October, at approximately 4:56pm and is expected to continue until further notice.

In addition to the delays on the Rochdale line, no trams are currently operating on the Eccles, Trafford Centre, and Altrincham lines. Passengers may need to use alternative transport options, including express shuttle buses, trains, or Bee Network buses to complete their journeys.

Furthermore, there are ongoing delays on the Eccles line due to a previous road traffic collision, with tickets and passes valid on several bus routes, including the 10, 30, 33, 50, 52, 53, 67, 79, 100, 248, and 249 services.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys ahead of time and can contact the Metrolink customer service for assistance, especially as the lift at Besses o' th' Barn tram stop is out of service. The contact number for the Metrolink is 0161 244 1000, available from 7am to 8pm on weekdays and 8am to 8pm on weekends and bank holidays.

articles.title: Rochdale-London train service proposal rejected by regulator
articles.excerpt: The Office of Rail and Road has rejected plans for a direct train service between Rochdale and London Euston, disappointing local MP Paul Waugh and rail operator Lumo.
articles.content_html:
The Office of Rail and Road (ORR) has rejected a proposal for a new train service between Rochdale and London Euston, which aimed to provide four daily return services. The decision has been met with disappointment from Rochdale's MP Paul Waugh and the rail operator Lumo, who had hoped to launch the service by 2028.

The ORR stated that the additional services could increase the risk of delays spreading across the network, ultimately worsening reliability for all passengers. In a statement, Paul Waugh expressed his deep disappointment, highlighting the significance of the service for residents in Rochdale and the surrounding borough. He remains committed to improving transport connections with both Manchester and London.

Waugh noted that there are still reasons for optimism regarding future rail developments. He mentioned the Bee Network, which is set to enhance local rail services across Greater Manchester starting in 2028, and the government's ongoing efforts with Northern Powerhouse Rail, which aims to improve capacity on the West Coast Main Line.

The ORR also rejected similar applications from Wrexham, Shropshire & Midlands Railway Company for Wrexham-London services and Avanti West Coast for additional Blackpool-Euston services. A spokesperson for Lumo indicated that they are considering their next steps following the ORR's decision.

evidence_sources.captured_text: ‘Disappointment’ following Rochdale-London train idea rejected | Roch Valley Radio On Air Live now — track details aren't available right now Listen Live Watch ‘Disappointment’ following Rochdale-London train idea rejected George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter October 10, 2026 | 8:42 AM Print Land around Rochdale Station The decision to axe the idea for trains between Rochdale and London Euston is ‘disappointing’, says the town’s MP and rail operator. The idea to have four daily return services between Rochdale and London was rejected by the Office of Rail and Road (ORR). The reason given was that the additional services could ‘increase the risk of delays spreading and making reliability of the network worse for all passengers’. Low-cost rail operator Lumo had hoped to start services by 2028, with the plans receiving the backing of Rochdale MP Paul Waugh. Both shared their disappointment following the announcement. Paul Waugh, Rochdale’s MP, said: “I am deeply disappointed that the ORR has rejected the proposal for a direct Rochdale to London service. I know how much this would have meant to people in Rochdale and the wider borough, and I remain committed to improving our connections with both Manchester and London. “There are reasons to be hopeful about the future. The Bee Network is bringing greater integration of local rail services across Greater Manchester from 2028 onwards, while the government is progressing Northern Powerhouse Rail and has set out its long-term intention to develop a new rail connection between Birmingham and Manchester to increase capacity on the West Coast Main Line. “These are important investments in our rail network, and I will continue to make the case for Rochdale to benefit from better and more reliable transport links, including to London.” The ORR explained that gaps in the current timetable provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers. The government body concluded that adding more services into these windows would reduce that resilience and increase risk of disruption. The ORR also rejected the application of Wrexham, Shropshire & Midlands Railway Company (WSMR) for four return Wrexham-London Euston services and Avanti West Coast’s application for additional Blackpool-Euston services. A spokesperson for FirstGroup, who run the Lumo operation, said: “We are disappointed that the ORR has declined our revised application for new Lumo services between London and Rochdale, and we are considering our next steps. “Following the initial decision, we amended our plans in line with feedback and believe the revised proposal demonstrated strong economic benefits for passengers and communities. “It would have delivered the benefits of competition, including greater choice, lower fares and new opportunities for growth across Manchester and the north west. “Open access services have an important role to play in improving connectivity, attracting more people to rail and supporting economic development, all at no cost to the public purse. “We remain convinced that this route offered a compelling case for investment and long-term benefits for communities, businesses and the wider regional economy.” ORR has approved access for Avanti’s weekday 19:29 Chester to Euston service to carry passengers until December 2030. This train already runs as a fully crewed empty service so does not add another train to the route, but will benefit passengers, says the ORR. Stephanie Tobyn, ORR’s director of strategy, policy and reform, said: “New services, destinations and greater choice can bring real benefits for passengers and communities. But the West Coast Main Line is already under significant pressure, with performance reflecting limited resilience on a heavily used part of the rail network. “Our detailed analysis has shown that adding more trains to the current timetable would reduce the ability to recover when disruption occurs, increasing the risk of delays spreading and making reliability of the network worse for all passengers.” Add Roch Valley Radio as a preferred source on Google News to see more of our local reporting Add as a preferred source on Google Do you have a story for us? articles.title: No trains between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria this week as replacement buses run
articles.excerpt: Passengers travelling between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are being advised to allow extra time this week, with trains replaced by buses from Monday 10 to Friday 14 August.
articles.content_html:
Rail passengers travelling between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are facing disruption this week, with no train service operating on the route from Monday 10 August to Friday 14 August 2026 because of planned engineering work.

Rail replacement buses are operating between Manchester Victoria and Rochdale. Passengers can use a direct replacement service or a stopping service calling at Moston, Mills Hill and Castleton. Travellers making the full journey between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are advised to use the direct replacement bus where possible.

The disruption has prompted concern locally after passengers checking journeys discovered that their usual trains had been replaced. One post in the Rochdale Borough Noticeboard Facebook group said: ‘Just noticed there are no trains from Rochdale to Manchester this week, only replacement buses.’

The closure forms part of planned engineering work affecting services into and out of Manchester Victoria. Other Calder Valley services are operating to revised timetables, so passengers travelling beyond Rochdale should check their individual journey before setting off.

Replacement buses generally take longer than the normal rail journey and passengers should leave additional time, particularly during busy commuting periods. Anyone with onward connections is advised to check the latest timetable before travelling.

The disruption is currently scheduled to continue through Friday 14 August, with passengers advised to check National Rail or their train operator for the latest journey information before setting off.
